title: Fraudulent Android app detection: a systematic framework based on multi-dimensional behavioral characteristics
abstract: Abstract Fraudulent Android applications have become the primary vector for online financial fraud, while existing detection methods remain ineffective against three adversarial techniques: (1) TLS 1.3 with certificate pinning, which blocks traffic interception; (2) environment-aware evasion, which disables malicious payloads in sandboxes; (3) rapid code obfuscation and repackaging, which shorten the effective window of static signatures. This paper presents a unified detection framework that counters these evasions through three dimensions. First, we design an evasion-aware dynamic sandbox that integrates kernel-level eBPF traffic interception with transparent TLS decryption. Second, we build a multi-dimensional behavioral graph (SDK-Permission-API) that captures hidden intent chains invisible to static analysis. Third, a time-decay risk propagation algorithm, termed RiskRank, is applied to a threat knowledge graph of 15,247 entities that jointly considers behavioral weight, graph association, and sample recency, improving the detection of fast-evolving fraud. We evaluate the framework on 2000 real-world Android applications, comprising 1000 fraudulent and 1000 benign samples, of which 68% are packed or obfuscated. Our system achieves 96.8% detection accuracy and 98.6% AUC-ROC, outperforming 6 state-of-the-art baselines by 8–16 percentage points. The system processes a sample in 128s on average, supporting 32 concurrent analyses for operational deployment.

title: A dynamic malware detection method based on multi-modal features
abstract: Abstract The rapid increase of sophisticated malware poses significant challenges to existing detection methods. To address the challenge, we propose a dynamic malware detection method based on multi-modal features. This approach utilizes two distinct modalities from in-band and out-of-band: the API (Application Programming Interface) sequence features obtained in sandbox, and the image features converted by memory dump files obtained out of VM (Virtual Machine). A multi-modal deep learning model is proposed to fuse these features to distinguish sophisticated malware. Experiments show that our method is effective, achieving 98.6% accuracy on a dataset collected from VirusTotal and CNET. It demonstrates significant improvements over single-modal methods using either text or image features alone, while combining the advantages of out-of-band and in-band dynamic detection, providing an effective solution for malware detection.

title: VeriPriv: a privacy preserving attribute verification protocol for decentralized authentication
abstract: Abstract Attribute-based verification becomes more and more popular compared with identity-based authentication from the privacy point of view. Users can be authenticated by pieces of attributes rather than the whole identity. Attribute-based anonymous credential systems enable a user to prove possession of a given set of attributes to a verifier, without revealing information about other attributes. However, the challenge lies in how to securely prove the possession of attributes. In our paper, we propose a decentralized zero-knowledge protocol for attribute verification. There are three attribute verification modes, namely 1-out-of-n , n-out-of-n , and the Combined Verification Mode . The first two modes represent the "OR" and "AND" gates, while the Combined Verification Mode supports an OR of non-empty groups of AND attributes. We prove the security properties of the protocol in the security analysis. Meanwhile, we also outline some of the use-cases and applications of the proposed protocol, such as Internet of Things(IoT), federated learning and data validation.

title: TRINITY-IDS: a tri-view hybrid architecture with adaptive drift-evidential learning for robust and continual intrusion detection
abstract: The rapid evolution of cyber threats in modern network environments demands intelligent intrusion detection systems. This system should be capable of handling complex attack patterns and heterogeneous data distributions. Existing intrusion detection approaches mainly focus on statistical or temporal flow characteristics. This approach neglects the topological relationships among network entities and the uncertainty associated with detection decisions. In this work, a Tri-View Hybrid Architecture with Adaptive Drift-Evidential Learning (TRINITY-IDS) is proposed for robust intrusion detection. Initially, a Density-Aware Hybrid Resampling strategy based on Cluster-SMOTE and Edited Nearest Neighbor (ENN) cleaning is applied to overcome class imbalance and improve minority attack representation. An adversarial feature selection mechanism with gradient reversal learning is used to reduce dataset-specific feature leakage and enhance cross-domain generalization. The extracted features are represented through three complementary views: a statistical view using convolutional feature extraction with channel attention, a temporal view using speciality-token-augmented BiGRU with self-attention for sequential behavior modeling, and a topological view using Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to capture network relationship patterns. A dynamic cross-view adaptive fusion mechanism automatically learns the contribution of each representation for individual samples. In addition, a Dirichlet evidential learning head is used for uncertainty-aware attack classification. It estimates belief and uncertainty values rather than only deterministic predictions. To support evolving network conditions, an online Page-Hinkley drift detector and experience replay mechanism are incorporated for continual adaptation during streaming intrusion detection. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed TRINITY-IDS achieves an overall accuracy of 98.36%, precision of 98.26%, recall of 98.32%, and F1-score of 98.29%.

title: De Pace: Optimizing initial guesses for homomorphic reciprocal and square root evaluation with CKKS
abstract: Abstract Homomorphic encryption allows computation on encrypted data, making it a promising technology for privacy-preserving machine learning. However, currently available fully homomorphic schemes, such as CKKS, only support addition and multiplication by default. Modern applications, such as neural networks, require more complex functions, such as division and square root. This raises a performance question for CKKS: What is the most efficient way to implement division and square root using only addition and multiplication? For CKKS, additional constraints apply: commonly used methods, such as comparisons and bit shifts, are no longer permitted, rendering most existing literature unusable. Our work addresses this challenge by analyzing and improving the performance of the method best suited for homomorphic computation of division and square root: the Newton–Raphson method. Since the primary degree of freedom in Newton–Raphson is the initial value, we formulate the determination of the parameters for a suitable linear helper function as a black-box optimization problem and analyze how different approaches to choosing these parameters affect the performance of homomorphic square root and division computation. Specifically, we evaluate four selection methods: (1) brute-force, (2) simulated annealing, (3) hill climbing, and (4) gradient descent. Our results show that the best optimization method finds parameters with lower RMSE and lower multiplicative depth than brute-force search, while reducing parameter generation time by multiple orders of magnitude. Our contribution is the problem formulation and its systematic evaluation over 603 000 configurations, providing a practical reference on the accuracy and multiplicative depth that can be expected for a given interval and number of Newton iterations.

title: Causal-enhanced federated transfer learning framework for privacy-preserving cross-organizational strategic collaboration
abstract: Cross-organizational strategic collaboration increasingly demands data-driven coordination while confronting stringent privacy constraints and heterogeneous data distributions. This paper proposes a coupled framework integrating causal inference with federated transfer learning to enable effective knowledge sharing across organizational boundaries without centralizing sensitive data. The framework comprises three core components: a distributed causal discovery algorithm that reconstructs inter-organizational causal structures through secure aggregation protocols, a causal-enhanced federated transfer learning mechanism that identifies invariant features transferable across heterogeneous enterprise contexts, and an adaptive privacy computing architecture that dynamically allocates protection resources according to data sensitivity profiles. Experimental validation across multi-enterprise ecosystems demonstrates that the causal enhancement mechanism improves cross-domain generalization robustness by 43% compared to conventional federated transfer learning, while maintaining predictive accuracy within 6.2% of centralized approaches. The adaptive privacy architecture retains 93.7% of collaborative utility under meaningful privacy constraints, with membership inference attack success rates near random baseline. These results establish that properly designed federated frameworks can approach centralized performance while preserving organizational autonomy, enabling broader participation in data-driven strategic alliances across regulatory and competitive boundaries.

title: Attentive temporal patch filtering for explainable streaming intrusion detection in medical IoT traffic
abstract: Network traffic in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) forms an unbounded multivariate temporal sequence whose statistics shift across devices, protocols, and acquisition environments; detecting malicious segments within it is a streaming time-series classification problem constrained by bounded per-window latency, essential for temporally localized explanations, and robustness to distribution shift. This research work presents TAPX-Net, a window-local classifier that decomposes each traffic window into temporal patches, applies channel-attentive depthwise convolutional filtering, and models the patch sequence with stacked bidirectional recurrent layers before attention pooling and dual classification and reconstruction heads. Each window is classified independently, with recurrent states reset at every window boundary, making the model window-causal. A temporal attribution module (TAM) produces patch- and feature-level explanations through Integrated Gradients (IG), validated against a causal input-level ablation. A feature-harmonized adaptation stage transfers the trained model to new network environments through limited-label fine-tuning with Maximum Mean Discrepancy alignment. On the CICIoMT2024 benchmark, TAPX-Net reaches a recall of 0.9541 at an FPR of one percent and a zero-day recall of 0.8963 across ten held-out attack classes, exceeding 7 baselines on every detection metric, and under CPU-only inference on the tested configuration processes a continuous stream at 108.7 windows per second with 98.8 percent of decisions within a 10 ms per-window bound. IG tracks the causal ablation more closely than attention weights (AW) across all attack classes, and cross-dataset transfer (CDT) to the general-purpose UNSW-NB15 and ToN-IoT benchmarks recovers most of the achievable performance gain with 5,000 labeled target windows. The reconstruction head contributes a 7.46 percentage point improvement in zero-day recall, focused on the generalization regime.

title: An explainable XGBoost–MLP fusion framework for intrusion detection in 5G and beyond networks
abstract: Abstract Fifth-generation (5G) and beyond networks combine virtualization, network slicing, massive device connectivity, and multi-access edge computing, thereby increasing both service flexibility and cybersecurity exposure. This paper presents an explainable ensemble intrusion-detection framework that combines Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and a compact multilayer perceptron (MLP) through validation-controlled probability fusion. The framework also integrates class-imbalance handling, feature selection, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), and explanation-aware security actions. Evaluation on the public 5G-NIDD benchmark used a stratified 70:15:15 training-validation-test split, common preprocessing for all models, and validation-only hyperparameter and fusion-weight selection. On the fixed held-out test split used in the supplied experiment log, the ensemble achieved 99.3% accuracy, 99.2% precision, 99.1% recall, 99.1% F1-score, 99.7% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and a 0.9% false-positive rate. The corresponding 95% Wilson interval for accuracy was 99.21-−99.38%, which describes sampling uncertainty on this test split rather than random-seed variability. SHAP identified packet rate, flow duration, SYN behavior, destination-port entropy, source bytes, and connection state as influential global indicators, while LIME supported alert-level validation. Detection required 22.6 ms per flow after warm-up, whereas generating both SHAP and LIME explanations increased end-to-end latency to 83.3 ms. These measurements motivate a two-path deployment strategy: continuous low-latency edge detection and selective explanation generation for high-risk, uncertain, or policy-sensitive alerts. A fixed-test statistical analysis using Wilson confidence intervals and Holm-adjusted accuracy comparisons confirmed that the reported improvement over every baseline was significant at adjusted $$p<0.001$$ on the held-out sample; random-seed variability is stated separately as a limitation.

title: TRUSTED PASSIVE OPTICAL NETWORKS ACCESS AUTHENTICATION USING DISTANCE CONDITIONED BIT ERROR RATE FINGERPRINTING AND A PERMISSIONED BLOCKCHAIN
abstract: To address credential cloning and limited auditability in passive optical networks (PONs), we present a simulation-based proof of concept for access authentication that integrates distance-conditioned bit-error-rate (BER) fingerprinting with a permissioned blockchain.A BER-distance reference template is constructed under registered link conditions.During authentication, normalized deviations between real-time pre-forward-error-correction BER and registered references serve as channel fingerprints for physical-layer authentication, while an adaptive threshold, calibrated on simulated legitimate observations, assesses physical-path consistency.Nonce-bound signed measurement evidence supports auditable authorization through practical Byzantine fault tolerance consensus.On an independent simulated test set, the validation-selected threshold yields a false rejection rate of 0.493% and a false acceptance rate of 0.019%; the uncertainty-scaled, relative, and absolute BER-deviation measures yield area under the curve values of 0.99999, 0.99990, and 0.90524, respectively.The results support feasibility under the modeled conditions; hardware validation remains necessary, and compensation attacks limit BER-based discrimination.

title: Photonic qudit entanglement and its applications to quantum key distribution
abstract: Abstract High-dimensional quantum key distribution (QKD) based on entangled qudits has emerged as a promising route for advancing the performance and practicality of quantum communication. By extending beyond the qubit framework, qudit entanglement enables the encoding of multiple bits per particle and offers greater robustness against noise, loss, and eavesdropping. In this review, we present qudit-based entanglement QKD protocols and their experimental demonstrations. We first introduce the basic concepts of qudits and provide an overview of foundational qubit-based entanglement QKD schemes, such as Ekert '91 (E91) and Bennett–Brassard–Mermin '92 (BBM92), which establish the core principles of entanglement-based secure key generation. Subsequently, we examine the generalization of these protocols to entangled qudits, highlighting how higher dimensionality enhances secure key rates and noise tolerance. Finally, we survey experimental demonstrations of qudit-based entanglement QKD across photonic platforms and outline prospects, showing that high-dimensional entanglement can be reliably generated, distributed, and measured for QKD with high stability and scalability. Remarkably, these achievements not only verify the feasibility of practical high-dimensional QKD, but also demonstrate clear advantages over qubit-based systems. Overall, theoretical frameworks and experimental realizations reviewed here position photonic qudit-based entanglement QKD as a promising resource for scalable, high-speed, and secure quantum communication networks, unveiling its potential as a central component in the future of quantum information technologies.

title: Impact of dephased entanglement, mixed input states and varying measurement orientations on the reliability of cryptographic keys generated via the quantum protocol E91
abstract: Photons and optical circuits are among the most promising platforms for implementation of quantum technologies, including quantum computing and quantum cryptography. For entanglement-based quantum key distribution, on-demand sources of highly entangled photon pairs are essential, and semiconductor quantum dots have emerged as prominent candidates to satisfy the necessary conditions of brightness and fidelity. However, in most cases the photon pair emitted by these sources is an anomalous Bell state whose relative phase and purity are non-ideal, and then, their suitability for distributing secret keys must be assessed. This work studies the performance of the quantum key distribution protocol E91, under the influence of three elements: the phase in the input state, the impurity of such a state, and the relative directions of the polarization analyzers. We derive analytical expressions for the minimum quantum bit error rate and the Bell’s parameter, and validate them by using quantum computational tools. Our results show that the performance of the quantum transmission is highly impacted by the phase and purity of the entangled input states, and that such an impact may be modulated through the orientation of the polarizers. These findings provide important insight for the scalable implementation of quantum key distribution protocols with realistic entanglement sources.

title: Fuzzy trust-based secure localization with CNN intrusion detection and RANSAC-GDA for wireless sensor networks
abstract: Abstract Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have made possible many applications like environment tracking, healthcare, smart cities, etc. However, reliable node localization remains challenging due to energy constraints, noisy range estimates, and malicious adversaries. This paper proposes a hybrid secure and energy-efficient localization framework that integrates Distributed Energy-Efficient Clustering (DEEC), Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC), and a Gaussian Distribution Approach (GDA) to enable robust position estimation. In addition, a lightweight Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on a SMOTE-assisted Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is deployed at the pre-localization stage to identify and exclude malicious nodes, including Sybil behavior and falsified localization information. DEEC-RANSAC-GDA facilitates energy-efficient selection for cluster head formation, mitigates localization outliers via RANSAC, and optimizes localization using Gaussian probabilistic models. Implementation of the proposed IDS on the CIC-IDS-2017 benchmark dataset achieved 99.83% accuracy, 99.00% precision, 99.84% recall, and 99.42% F1-score, along with minimizing localization errors falling within the range of 0.46 m-0.53 m compared to DV-Hop and Weighted Hyperbolic Localization schemes.

title: Fast few-shot intrusion detection via depthwise meta-learning
abstract: Network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) increasingly rely on deep learning to cope with evolving cyber attacks, yet they typically require large amounts of labeled data per attack type and exhibit poor generalization to novel threats. Recent advances in meta-learning and few-shot learning have shown promise for alleviating data scarcity, while depthwise separable convolutions (DSC) offer a computationally efficient means of extracting fine-grained spatial–temporal features from network traffic. In this paper, we propose a meta-learning framework for few-shot network intrusion detection that combines a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) objective with a one-dimensional DSC backbone. Tasks are defined episodically across attack families and datasets, enabling the meta-learner to acquire an initialization that rapidly adapts to unseen attack types using only a handful of labeled flows. We derive the corresponding bilevel optimization problem, analyze the computational benefits of DSC compared with standard convolutions, and present an end-to-end architecture tailored for flow-based NIDS. Experiments on CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 under challenging 5-shot and 10-shot settings demonstrate consistent improvements in accuracy and macro- $$F_1$$ over strong convolutional, metric-based and attention-enhanced baselines inspired by recent literature. The proposed approach reduces parameters by up to 65% relative to conventional convolutions while maintaining or improving detection performance. We conclude with a discussion of limitations and directions for integrating cross-domain adaptation and self-attention into meta-learned DSC architectures.

title: FHE-Assisted Privacy-Preserving Medical Image De-Identification
venue: Journal of Emerging Technologies With Industrial Applications
abstract: Medical image de-identification is essential for data sharing, but conventional OCR-based redaction can expose protected health information (PHI) to the service that performs redaction. We present a client-cloud framework that applies fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) to privacy-preserving medical image de-identification. The client localizes text, segments character patches, encrypts normalized inputs with CKKS, and performs final correction and masking, while the cloud evaluates an FHE-compatible VGG-style character recognizer and CharCNN PHI classifier over ciphertexts. The system reduces encrypted inference cost through polynomial activations, average pooling, diagonal encoding, Toeplitz-style convolution lowering, and BSGS rotation reuse. Prototype results show 100%plaintext-ciphertext prediction consistency, 83.15%corrected character accuracy, and 97.1% encrypted PHI-classification accuracy, with bootstrapped nonlinear layers remaining the main bottleneck.

title: Enhanced multiclass intrusion detection on imbalanced IoT NetFlow traffic using a three-tier stacked time-distributed LSTM with SMOTENC-based class balancing
abstract: The network-based attack surface has flourished abruptly with the unveiling of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. As a result, there is a pressing demand for automated intrusion detection systems (IDS) that can reliably identify a variety of attacks with severe class imbalance. Deep recurrent models are suitable for NetFlow traffic, however, a single-layer long short-term memory (LSTM) network is often inadequate for separating minority attack classes, and the effect of oversampling and model size is not well quantified. This study presents a three-tier stacked Time-Distributed long short-term memory network (ST-LSTM) evaluated on NF-BoT-IoT (600,100 flows, four attack classes and one benign class) under a leakage-free protocol. Ten flow features serve as predictors, while the class label and host identifiers are excluded. The data are divided into training, validation and test partitions before any fitting, and mixed-type oversampling (SMOTENC) is applied to the training partition only, at a ratio selected on validation data. On the untouched test set of 120,020 flows, the model reaches 83.98% accuracy, 0.8500 weighted F1, 0.6609 macro F1 and 0.9678 weighted ROC-AUC, the highest values among classical, shallow recurrent and stacked-ensemble baselines, and five-fold cross-validation gives 83.94 ± 0.19% accuracy. Standard SMOTE, by contrast, creates invalid protocol and flag codes and suppresses DDoS detection. A label-conflict analysis shows that 99.9% of DDoS and DoS flows share identical feature vectors with other classes, which limits attainable five-class accuracy to 84.91%, the model reaches 98.9% of this bound, and nearly all of its remaining errors fall on these ambiguous flows.

title: Effective channel representations and composable security for passive-user Loop-Back quantum key distribution
abstract: Abstract This work develops effective channel representations and a composable-security framework for distributed passive-user Loop-Back quantum key distribution (QKD). Alice provides trusted preparation-and-measurement infrastructure at local service points, while two source-free and detector-free users, $$B_1$$ and $$B_2$$ , apply independently selected polarization rotations $$R(\pm \pi /8)$$ to the same optical carrier. Two complementary derivations describe the honest operation. Direct averaging over the composed rotations gives the observable Loop-Back map, while an operationally equivalent representation on the Bennett–Brassard 1984 (BB84) preparation-and-measurement data is a balanced mixture of conjugate-basis dephasings, or an anisotropic Pauli channel with identity, $$X$$ , and $$Z$$ components and no $$Y$$ component. Both recover the ideal conclusive-event probability $$P_{\textrm{conc}}=1/4$$ . Security is established without restricting the adversarial action to this effective channel. Eve may implement an arbitrary coherent attack with quantum memory on the single untrusted interface between the two local rotations. In the single-photon sector, a Choi-operator identity yields the exact ideal relation $$e_{1,\mathrm p}=3e_{1,\mathrm b}/2$$ , together with a low-error robust angular bound $$e_{1,\mathrm p}\le \kappa _{\textrm{rot}}e_{1,\mathrm b}$$ . Phase-randomized weak coherent pulses, decoy-state estimation and generalized entropy accumulation then give a finite-key composable bound. A common optical model compares asymptotic and finite-block rates and quantifies their convergence with block size. The analysis also identifies the trusted-interface condition required to exclude loss-assisted operation-discrimination attacks and specifies the hardware assumptions needed for optical implementation.

title: Concurrency aware artificial intelligence for real-time intrusion detection in software-defined networks
abstract: Contemporary software systems are now being used in environments that are highly concurrent, data-intensive, and latency-sensitive. Software-Defined Networks (SDNs) applications like real-time intrusion detection need fast pattern recognition in large amounts of data streams through time. Although deep learning models have impressive detection capabilities, failure to perform well in real-world deployments is usually limited by poor concurrency management, inflexible scheduling, centralized learning pipelines, and fault tolerance. In this study, the authors suggest a concurrency-aware artificial intelligence (CA-AI) framework that directly incorporates actor-based concurrency control, workflow-based load-aware scheduling, deep long short-term memory (LSTM)-based temporal learning, agent-based parallel feature extraction, and feedback loops based on monitoring. The framework is evaluated for SDN-oriented intrusion detection workloads, where concurrency management is implemented at the system architecture level through actor-based execution, workflow scheduling, and asynchronous inference and tested on real network traffic data samples (NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, and UNSW-NB15). Experimental results demonstrate that concurrency-aware system design leads to a significant improvement in the detection accuracy achieving up to 98.9% detection accuracy across multiple benchmark datasets, including NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, and UNSW-NB15, throughput improved by 2.1 × compared with the centralized IDS baseline, while throughput increased by approximately 1.19 × when concurrency increased from 10,000 to 100,000 flows within the proposed CA-AI framework, average latency was reduced by approximately 57.5% compared with the centralized IDS baseline (146 ms to 62 ms), while maintaining high reliability under concurrent workloads. The proposed framework establishes concurrency as a fundamental architectural principle for scalable AI-driven pattern recognition systems.

title: Classification of network security attacks using novel enhanced restricted Boltzmann machine-based bitterling fish optimization algorithm
abstract: In the past, intrusion detection was mostly dependent on established techniques like protocol control, anti-virus software models, firewalls, and the encryption-decryption approach. Although these techniques were effective in detecting a small count of attacks, they had trouble detecting many attacks and had a significant false positive rate. But when harmful attacks get larger, new problems arise that require an all-encompassing reaction. Hence, this article plans to perform network security attack classification using novel intelligent deep learning techniques. Initially, the data is gathered from the standard benchmark datasets, such as the CICIDS 2017 and CSE-CICIDS 2018 datasets. The collected data undergoes pre-processing using the Min-Max normalization method. Next, the features are extracted from these pre-processed data using the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method. These extracted features undergo the final classification stage using the novel Enhanced Restricted Boltzmann Machine (ERBM), in which the parameter tuning of RBM is accomplished by the nature inspired optimization algorithm referred as Bitterling Fish Optimization (BFO) algorithm with the intention of accuracy maximization as the major fitness function. This novel ERBM-BFO classifies the final output into various attacks, such as normal, DoS attack, DDoS attack, brute force attack, botnet attack, web attack, infiltration attack, and port scan attack, respectively. The outcomes suggested that the method is effective and suitable for identifying attacks in contemporary situations. The proposed ERBM-BFO method for the network security classification model in terms of accuracy is 9.35%, 6.85%, 4.47%, and 2.19% better than LSTM + AE, CNN+LSTM, MLP, and RBM, respectively. Similarly, the proposed ERBM-BFO method for the network security classification model with respect to recall is 9.44%, 6.92%, 4.51%, and 2.20% advanced than LSTM + AE, CNN+LSTM, MLP, and RBM, respectively.

title: Certificateless universal designated-verifier signature proofs for carbon-footprint verification
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
abstract: Abstract Carbon-footprint audits require organizations to verify signed electricity and production evidence while limiting unnecessary disclosure. We study a certificateless signature-proof construction that combines a partial key issued by a key-generation center (KGC), an independent user secret, signature transformation and an interactive proof of the transformation factor. A canonical message binds the report and evidence digests to the signer identity, key epoch and accounting context; detailed records remain off chain. For validated nonidentity statements, we establish correctness, two-transcript signature extraction and honest-verifier transcript simulation. These properties are distinguished from the additional unforgeability requirements of the underlying signature. Reproducible analytical calculations describe communication size, group-operation counts, queueing and ledger-dependent workflow latency. Under explicitly selected delay inputs, an asynchronous online decision is calculated at 385.2 ms, compared with 2570.2 ms when commitment blocks the same path. These values are model outputs, not measured cryptographic or deployment performance. Source attestation, endpoint key protection, revocation and constrained-device verification are discussed as deployment measures. The result is a bounded design and analytical assessment; a complete underlying-signature security proof and implementation measurements remain necessary for deployment.

title: Blockchain-enhanced SDN framework with deep unfolding spatial frequency attention network and pine cone optimization for smart city IoT cybersecurity
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) in smart cities has revolutionized services by connecting numerous devices to deliver intelligent applications. However, this interconnected environment also exposes IoT networks to severe cybersecurity risks, including data breaches, intrusions, and advanced persistent threats. Traditional detection mechanisms often struggle with high-dimensional traffic, noisy data, missing values, and evolving attack patterns, which significantly reduce their reliability. Moreover, ensuring secure and tamper-proof storage of detection outcomes in large-scale IoT system s remains a major challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-enhanced IoT cybersecurity framework for smart cities, utilizing a software-defined networking framework with a Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network and Pine Cone Optimization (DUSFAN-PCO). Initially, input data is collected from UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS2017 datasets. The collected data are pre-processed using Diffusion Models for Missing Value Imputation (DMMVI) to handle noise and missing values. Next, Carpet Weaver Optimization (CWO) is applied to select the most informative attributes. These selected features are then fed into the Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network (DUSFAN), which classifies IoT network traffic into normal and multiple attack categories through real-time anomaly detection. To further enhance detection accuracy, Pine Cone Optimization (PCO) is used to fine-tune DUSFAN’s weight parameters. Finally, the results are securely stored and managed using a Blockchain-Based Secure PBFT Lightweight Consensus (SPBFT-LC), ensuring immutability, transparency, and trust among IoT nodes. The proposed DUSFAN-PCO framework achieves an accuracy of 99.20% on UNSW-NB15 and 99.48% on CIC-IDS2017, with F1-scores of 99.52% and 99.50%, and ROC values of 0.99–1.00 across both datasets. Coupled with high blockchain-based security integrity (> 99%), it ensures robust, real-time, and reliable detection of IoT network intrusions, making it highly suitable for secure and resilient smart city IoT environments.

title: Review of System Design Approaches in Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Security Operations Centers
abstract: Security operations centers increasingly rely on agentic artificial intelligence systems, which combine large language model reasoning with tool invocation and multi-step planning, to automate alert triage, investigation, and response. Independent research groups have proposed structurally distinct architectures for this purpose, ranging from single-agent reasoning loops to multi-agent systems with shared context or deterministic safety constraints, but no publication has systematically compared these designs against a common set of criteria. This review addresses that gap by constructing a five-dimension classification framework covering agent cardinality, coordination mechanism, autonomy boundary, safety enforcement layer, and validation maturity. A corpus of published systems relevant to security operations was retrieved from academic preprint archives and conference proceedings and coded against this framework. Five recurring design patterns were identified, together with the available quantitative evidence comparing them, including a controlled trial showing that multi-agent orchestration produced consistently reliable recommendations while single-agent approaches did not. The analysis found that claimed autonomy consistently outpaced empirical validation across the reviewed designs, with most systems evaluated no further than a single organizational deployment despite permitting autonomous action. These findings indicate that validation maturity should be assessed independently from architectural sophistication when organizations evaluate agentic artificial intelligence for security operations, and they identify calibration and human oversight effectiveness as priority areas for future empirical study.

title: Reliable Entropy Estimation from Observed Statistics for Device-Independent Quantum Cryptography
abstract: We introduce a numerical framework for reliably estimating conditional von Neumann entropies, a central quantity in device-independent quantum cryptography and randomness generation. Our method is based on semidefinite relaxations derived from the Navascués--Pironio--Acín hierarchy and provides entropy bounds directly from observed statistics, assuming only the validity of quantum mechanics. The approach builds on a recent integral representation of entropy and substantially improves efficiency: it requires about half as many support variables as existing methods, while allowing these variables to be chosen projectively, leading to a significant reduction in runtime. These advances enable the practical certification of randomness and security even in noisy conditions, while integrating seamlessly with modern entropy accumulation theorems. Consequently, our framework becomes a versatile tool for quantum cryptographic protocols, broadening the possibilities for secure communication in untrusted environments.

title: Quantum secret sharing in a tripartite superconducting network
abstract: Superconducting microwave quantum networks is a rapidly developing field, enabling distributed quantum computing and holding a promise for hybrid architectures in quantum internet. Quantum secret sharing (QSS) is one of the key protocols for multipartite quantum networks and can provide an unconditionally secure way to share quantum states among $n$ players. Using microwave two-mode squeezed states as an entanglement resource, we experimentally implement a QSS protocol with $n = 3$, where a subset of at least $k = 2$ players must collaborate to faithfully reconstruct the original secret state. We demonstrate reconstructed-state fidelities that surpass the asymptotic no-cloning threshold of $F_\textrm{nc} = 2/3$ and identify a parameter regime that allows for unconditionally secure communication in the presence of an omnipotent dishonest player. Furthermore, we experimentally explore inherent connections between QSS and other important quantum information processing tasks, such as quantum dense coding and elementary quantum error correction of channel erasures. Finally, we discuss extensions of QSS and its relation to the concept of blind quantum computing.

title: ON-PREMISE OPEN-WEIGHT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS FOR INTERPRETABLE WEB VULNERABILITY DETECTION: A BENCHMARK AGAINST CLOUD MODELS AND RULE-BASED STATIC ANALYSIS
abstract: Organisations handling regulated or proprietary source code are frequently prohibited from transmitting it to third-party inference providers, which excludes commercial cloud large language models from their security-analysis pipelines regardless of the accuracy those models achieve. Whether self-hosted open-weight models can substitute for them on ordinary developer hardware has not been established. This study benchmarks five quantised open-weight models, from 1.5 to 8 billion parameters and executed entirely on a consumer laptop graphics processor with eight gigabytes of video memory, on 120 annotated web-application code snippets spanning five weakness categories. Each was evaluated under zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting and compared against a rule-based static analyser and previously published cloud-model results on the identical corpus. The strongest local configuration reached an F1-score of 0.900, exceeding the previous-generation cloud flagship and trailing the current one by 4.7 points, while generating a remediation suggestion for every correct detection. The analysis further shows that F1 alone conceals degenerate behaviour: several configurations, including one cloud model, approach the score of a classifier labelling every input as vulnerable, so reporting specificity alongside F1 is proposed as a minimum requirement. Privacy-preserving on-premise vulnerability analysis is thus attainable without specialised infrastructure.

title: MODIFIKASI METODE CHINESE REMINDER THEOREM MENGGUNAKAN BLUM BLUM SHUB GENERATOR UNTUK PEMBENTUKAN WATERMARKING CITRA DIGITAL
venue: JITSI Jurnal Informatika Dan Teknologi Sistem Informasi
abstract: Data security is an essential aspect of information technology development, particularly in the exchange and distribution of digital information. Digital images, especially personal photographs, are vulnerable to misuse by unauthorized parties. One technique that can be used to enhance information security in digital images is watermarking, which involves embedding specific information into an image as a means of data protection. The Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) is one of the methods that can be applied in the watermark embedding process. However, the application of this method may pose security risks if the embedding pattern can be identified by unauthorized parties. Therefore, modifications are needed to improve the security of the watermark embedding process. This study aims to modify the CRT method by integrating the Blum Blum Shub Generator (BBS) algorithm to randomize data embedding locations in digital images. The BBS algorithm is used to generate random numbers that serve as the basis for determining pixel positions where the watermark is embedded. This approach makes the embedding locations more difficult to predict, thereby reducing the risk of watermark detection and extraction by unauthorized parties. This modification is expected to enhance watermark embedding security while preserving the visual imperceptibility of the image, ensuring that the changes are not easily noticeable to the naked eye. Thus, the combination of the CRT method and the BBS algorithm is expected to provide an alternative approach to improving the protection of information embedded in digital images

title: Enhancing IoT network security with self-supervised multi-residual attention graph networks
abstract: An Intrusion Detection System is crucial for securing Internet of Things. The conventional Intrusion Detection System technologies face challenges in detecting minority-class intrusions due to class imbalance and limited ability to model intricate dependencies in network traffic. To address these challenges, this research provides an intelligent framework to detect network intrusion in an Internet of Things network named Self-Supervised Multi-Residual Attention Graph Network (SS-MRAGNet). Specifically, SS-MRAGNet integrates node and edge aggregation with a multi-residual attention mechanism to learn complex structural dependencies within network traffic data. The framework incorporates self-supervised pre-training with pseudo-labeling and edge augmentation to address the class imbalance challenges and detect minority-class intrusions accurately. A minimal Random Under Sampling strategy is applied only within training folds to stabilize optimization, without serving as the primary imbalance-handling mechanism. Then, the model performs iterative self-training to generate high-confidence predictions, which are then used to pseudo-label unlabeled data. After the iterative process, predictions are refined. Rademacher complexity framework and convergence proofs are utilized for theoretical analysis to analyze its performance in noisy and imbalanced data. On validation, CIC-Darknet2020, CSE-CIC-IDS2018, UNSW_NB15, and Ton-IoT datasets result in 98.25% accuracy, 98.21%, precision, 98% recall, and 98.1% F1-score, outperforming state-of-the-art models. Complexity analysis further demonstrates its suitability for near real-time deployment at the fog/gateway level. This study proposes a novel graph-based IDS framework and provides practical insights into handling class imbalance, highlighting its potential for secure and scalable IoT intrusion detection.

title: EVIDENCE-INFORMED CROSS-LAYER SECURITY RECOMMENDATIONS FOR WIRELESS NETWORKS AND IOT DEVICES BASED ON PENETRATION TESTING
abstract: Smart-city and smart-home systems rely heavily on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, and ZigBee, while many practical risks arise from deployment and implementation weaknesses rather than failures of cryptographic primitives. This paper presents a structured, author-led synthesis of seven previously completed laboratory studies involving adaptive Wi-Fi penetration testing, WPA3-Enterprise attacks, a cross-layer audit of a commercial Wi-Fi smart lock, reverse analysis of a BLE control channel, cross-layer ZigBee assessment, software-defined-radio jamming, and an IoT security laboratory task set. The previously reported experimental findings are normalized by affected layer, attack vector, observable effect, test conditions, and source. On this basis, the study develops a six-level cross-layer taxonomy and 52 stakeholder-oriented recommendations for infrastructure administrators, device and firmware developers, mobile and cloud service developers, monitoring and risk-assessment teams, and testing-process owners. Each recommendation is assigned an evidence level distinguishing direct experimental support, support from external standards or literature, and proposed expert guidance. Priority controls are linked to reproducible acceptance criteria and twelve core metrics, while an extended traceability matrix provides qualitative or quantitative checks for the remaining recommendations. The resulting five-stage procedure is proposed as a testing-remediation-re-verification framework; it has not yet been independently validated as a complete system on an industrial testbed. The contribution is therefore an evidence-informed operational framework rather than a claim that all controls or thresholds are universally validated.

title: BMSVP: Blockchain-based message signing and verification protocol for security enhancement in smart grids
abstract: Abstract The transformation of traditional power grid systems towards smart grids is driven by factors such as the expansion of vehicle charging infrastructure, rapid technological advancements, demands for energy efficiency, as well as the surge in distributed energy generation. However, the smart grid system integrates with numerous internet of things (IoT) devices and legacy systems, most of which have inherent vulnerabilities or do not support current cryptographic protocols. In addition, the communication among the myriad of smart grid devices takes place over the public internet, further exposing the smart grids to security threats. Although numerous security techniques have been presented to mitigate these threats, the provision of perfect security at low overheads remains elusive. In this paper, we leverage blockchain, bilinear pairings, and elliptic curve cryptography to develop a provably secure protocol for smart grids. Its formal security is performed using the widely deployed Real or Random (RoR) model, while its semantic security analysis demonstrate its resilience against threats such as side-channeling, replays and privileged insiders. In addition, it is shown to offer authentication, untraceability, anonymity, and perfect key secrecy. In terms of performance evaluation, it is shown to reduce communication costs by 22.36% while maintaining fairly low computation overheads. There is therefore a need to further optimize this protocol to lessen the incurred computation overheads.

title: Automated Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Malware Obfuscation on Compiled Binaries
abstract: Obfuscation is routinely applied to malicious code, yet its effectiveness is usually argued rather than measured. In practice it is assessed by the drop in the number of engines that flag a sample – a figure that changes as signature databases do. Existing quantitative frameworks measure the program instead, but operate on source code and cannot be applied to the samples an analyst receives. This paper presents an automated pipeline that measures obfuscation quality on compiled Windows binaries and reports two quantities: an index Q of the cost imposed on analysis and a separate measure S of how much of the original byte sequence survives. Every sample is verified by execution, and the pipeline was applied to thirteen purpose-built modules under ten transformation combinations, giving 130 verified pairs. Over these pairs Q and S prove not to be interchangeable – their relationship reverses direction depending on whether transformations are compared on one sample or samples are compared with each other. The clipped normalisation of relative change in common use reaches its ceiling as soon as a measured quantity doubles, so it assigns its maximum to four fifths of the dataset although the underlying structural growth spans two orders of magnitude; a logarithmic normalisation restores the distinction. And no transformation removes a single imported function: the import table is produced by the linker, beyond the reach of a source-level obfuscator, so the strongest static indicators available to a scanner survive any amount of added control-flow complexity.

title: A unified drift-adaptive and robust residual autoencoder with attention and few-shot learning for zero-day intrusion detection
abstract: Abstract Autoencoder-based unsupervised intrusion detection systems (IDS) offer a promising approach for identifying zero-day attacks without requiring labeled malicious data. However, residual autoencoder (RAE) frameworks remain limited by static decision thresholds, susceptibility to concept drift (CD), limited adversarial robustness, and restricted adaptability to emerging attack patterns. To address these limitations, we propose the Attention-Boosted Streaming Residual Autoencoder (ASRAE), a unified framework that integrates attention-enhanced representation learning, online CD detection with adaptive thresholding, benign-only adversarial training, post-identification few-shot meta-learning, and explainability through integrated gradients (IG). Experiments on UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 show that ASRAE outperforms the evaluated unsupervised baselines, achieving ROC-AUC values of 0.952, 0.940, and 0.931, respectively. Under the controlled simulated concept-drift setting, ASRAE maintains a ROC-AUC above 0.91, while adversarial evaluation using Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) demonstrates improved robustness to feature-space perturbations. The few-shot adaptation stage further enables adaptation to held-out attack families using only a small number of labeled samples while largely preserving benign reconstruction performance. ASRAE requires an average inference time of 9.2 ms per sample in the evaluated experimental environment. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of ASRAE across the benchmark, simulated-drift, adversarial, and few-shot adaptation settings.

title: Scalability bottlenecks in entanglement-based satellite quantum key distribution: downlink asymmetry, orbit dependence and finite-key effects
abstract: Space-based entanglement distribution, as the backbone of the quantum Internet, is poised to enable global quantum networking from infrastructure to application platforms. Satellite-based quantum key distribution (SatQKD), with the entanglement-based QKD protocol of Bennett, Brassard, and Mermin (BBM92), promises source-independent security, but faces a trinity of scalability bottlenecks in dual-downlink configurations. Specifically, asymmetric link characteristics are exacerbated by optical ground station (OGS) pair system parameter differences, while orbit-dependent metrics, e.g., transmission window duration, overpass interval, and trajectory repeatability, introduce finite secret key length (SKL) extraction considerations. Further, quantum satellites will be within the range of multiple OGS pairs, which requires efficient scheduling of SatQKD to prioritize links, mitigate cloud cover disturbance, and maximize finite SKL. Here, we develop a co-modeling framework of dual-downlink SatQKD to support orbital parameter selection and performance comparison for asymmetric system-optics (e.g., aperture diameter, extraneous counts) parameters. We clarify the distinct performance of the SKL extraction methods for Sun-synchronous orbits (SSO) and polar orbits. We further incorporate the finite BBM92 SKL analysis into downlink scheduling optimisation to truncate adverse data collection periods and explore the advantages in flexibility and efficiency for global networking. Our work provides actionable design insights for future entanglement-based global quantum communications.

title: Reliable Estimation of Differential Privacy under Selection Bias
abstract: Statistical privacy audits are essential for verifying the theoretical privacy guarantees of differentially private (DP) mechanisms. Auditors typically use Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) to estimate a lower bound on the true privacy leakage of DP mechanisms at a specified confidence level, which should not exceed the theoretical privacy upper bound guaranteed by DP. However, we found that many auditing implementations in prior work introduce a selection bias when running MIAs, which leads to statistically invalid and overestimated lower bounds. Because most audits are not tight, this bias has thus far gone unnoticed: the estimated lower bounds remained well below the theoretical upper bounds. Nevertheless, accurately evaluating this lower bound is critical, as a flawed statistical assessment could lead to false alarms on correct mechanisms or an incorrect evaluation of the guarantee's tightness. This work employs tools from the statistical literature to correct this bias. We present an overview of the different correction methods and assess their respective advantages. Furthermore, we perform a comprehensive re-analysis of results returned by prior audit implementations and show that without statistical correction, these audits violate the theoretical upper bounds up to four times more often than their claimed confidence level implies. With correction applied, the resulting lower bounds are statistically valid, and violations occur at no more than the nominal rate.

title: Redistricting from the bottom up: sampling communities of interest with differential privacy
MQTT-HS: A formally verified and proxy-mediated hybrid security protocol for MQTT-based IoT networks
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
abstract: Abstract MQTT enables efficient communication in resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) systems but does not provide integrated protection against cryptographic and behavioral threats. This paper presents MQTT-HS, a proxy-mediated security protocol that combines certificate-based authentication, ephemeral ECDH/HKDF session establishment, AES-256-GCM payload protection, controlled key refresh, and metadata-based hierarchical intrusion detection with inline enforcement. ProVerif verified the modeled secrecy, authentication, replay-resistance, message-flow agreement, and epoch-key secrecy properties of the cryptographic core. MQTT-HS supports forward secrecy across expired epochs through fresh ephemeral ECDH material, independent epoch-key derivation, and secure erasure of obsolete key material. An ESP32 implementation delivered all 360 protected messages and completed six in-session rekeys, with an average AES-256-GCM encryption latency of 0.354 ms per message. Controlled runtime experiments rejected all evaluated replay, untrusted-certificate, and invalid-signature attempts. The hierarchical XGBoost IDS achieved balanced accuracies of 0.808, 0.960, and 0.862 across its three stages, although Stage 0 produced a 37.5% false-positive rate on the limited legitimate holdout subset. Compared with the evaluated mutual TLS baselines, MQTT-HS preserved more endpoint free heap and provided MQTT-aware detection and enforcement, while requiring greater network bandwidth and a trusted Security Proxy. The results support the feasibility of MQTT-HS under the evaluated prototype configuration.

title: MACHINE LEARNING-BASED IDENTITY PATTERN ANALYSIS FOR INTELLIGENT CYBERSECURITY THREAT DETECTION
venue: International Journal of Data Science and IoT Management System
abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber threats has created a need for intelligent security systems capable of identifying suspicious user activities, unauthorized access, compromised accounts, and insider threats. Traditional cybersecurity mechanisms that rely primarily on predefined rules and known attack signatures may struggle to detect previously unseen threats and subtle deviations in user behaviour. Machine learning provides opportunities to analyse identity-related activity patterns and distinguish normal behaviour from potentially malicious actions. This research proposes a machine learning-based framework for identity pattern analysis and intelligent cybersecurity threat detection. The framework examines authentication records, login frequency, access histories, device information, session characteristics, and deviations from established user behaviour. Data preprocessing and feature engineering are used to prepare identity-related records for analysis, while supervised and unsupervised learning techniques are considered for threat classification and anomaly detection. Candidate algorithms include Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Isolation Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory networks for sequential behavioural data. The proposed framework will be evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1- score, false-positive rate, and computational efficiency. Explainability and privacy considerations will also be incorporated to support responsible security decisions. The study aims to develop an adaptive approach to identity-based threat detection that can assist organizations in identifying suspicious activities and strengthening access security. The effectiveness of the framework must be established through empirical experimentation using appropriate cybersecurity datasets.

title: Cybersecurity Performance of Shanghai Cooperation Organization Countries and Türkiye Using the Hybrid MEREC-MAUT Approach
abstract: Besides the benefits, digitalization has brought certain responsibilities and risks into everyday life.Cyberattacks, which are hard to predict, can cause serious harm to individuals, institutions, and countries.As a result, raising awareness about cybersecurity and assessing cybersecurity performance have become crucial.These threats, which have grown from regional to global issues, demand an analysis of the cybersecurity policies of international organizations and the capabilities of member states.This study aims to address a gap in regional cybersecurity evaluations by examining Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) member states alongside Türkiye, considering its strategic role as a dialogue partner.For this purpose, it introduces a novel hybrid MEREC-MAUT framework to offer a structured comparative assessment.The 2024 Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI) data were analyzed using a hybrid approach that combines MEREC (Method based on the Removal Effects of Criteria) and MAUT (Multi-Attribute Utility Theory).MEREC was selected for objective weighting based on criteria removal effects, while MAUT offers flexible utility-based ranking, providing a robust analytical approach over traditional multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) methods.The analysis indicated that 'technical measures' ranked as the top criterion, followed by capacity-development and organizational measures.Türkiye, India, and Pakistan emerged as the top-performing countries, whereas Tajikistan and Belarus exhibited the lowest performance by a significant margin.The empirical results highlight the critical importance of regional collaboration within the SCO and reveal that prioritizing technical measures is essential for boosting cybersecurity performance.Thus providing policy-makers with a strategic improvement roadmap for targeted infrastructure updates in underperforming nations.

title: An Explainable XGBoost-Based Intrusion Detection Framework for Cloud Security Using SHAP Analysis
abstract: With the proliferation of cloud-based services and the volume of data being stored and managed on this platform, businesses are exposed to new risks from cyber threats like Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, exploits, reconnaissance, malware communication and unauthorized access attempts. While conventional IDSs are less effective in detecting new attack patterns and typically are opaque in their decision making, they can prevent the occurrence of attacks.Traditional IDSs are generally opaque in their decision-making, and may be less effective in detecting new attack patterns, but they can be used to stop attacks from happening. To overcome such issues, this paper introduces an Explainable XGBoost Based Intrusion Detection Framework for Cloud Security Using SHAP Analysis. The methodology takes advantage of the dataset UNSW-NB15, which preprocesses network traffic records, encodes them and classifies them with a machine learning algorithm: XGBoost. Aimed at improving model interpretability, a new ingredient is added: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is incorporated to explain the role of individual features from the network to the classification results. The results of the experimental evaluation indicate that the proposed framework provides an overall accuracy of 95.13% and high values of precision, recall, and F1-score, which indicate the effectiveness of the framework in differentiating between malicious traffic and normal network behavior. The findings also indicate that explainable artificial intelligence can offer valuable insights into the decisions made for detecting attacks, which can boost trust and transparency in cloud security systems. Overall, the study demonstrates that XGBoost with SHAP is a promising and explainable approach for intrusion detection in today's cloud computing landscape.

title: A lightweight distributed intrusion detection framework for SDN via unsupervised feature augmentation and collaborative LightGBM
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Internet technologies, the Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, and software-defined networking (SDN) have emerged as key technologies for large-scale data processing in resource-constrained environments. However, the centralized control paradigm of SDN places substantial processing demands on a single controller, potentially resulting in excessive bandwidth overhead, high-dimensional data-processing challenges, and low computational efficiency. Moreover, the continuous data analytics and real-time policy enforcement required in heterogeneous networks further exacerbate controller-side performance bottlenecks. To address this issue, this study proposes a lightweight intrusion detection framework based on unsupervised representation learning and distributed collaborative learning, providing a potential perspective for achieving efficient classification in resource-constrained SDN environments. The principal contributions of this study are summarized as follows. (i) Unsupervised representation learning is employed to enrich the original feature space, while three complementary feature-selection strategies are used to identify the most informative features. This process preserves essential information while substantially reducing computational complexity. (ii) From a system-design perspective, the proposed framework exploits SDN programmability and the local processing capabilities of network nodes to distribute training tasks across individual nodes. This localized training architecture accelerates model training while effectively reducing communication overhead. (iii) Using only 13 key features selected from the original 83-dimensional feature set, the proposed method achieves an F1-score of 98.76%, with training times ranging from 9.65 to 13.65 seconds. These results demonstrate that the framework effectively balances detection performance and computational efficiency in distributed SDN environments. Overall, this study presents a lightweight distributed intrusion detection solution tailored to resource-constrained SDN environments.

title: Proof-of-Principle Implementation of Quantum Key Distribution in an Indefinite Causal Order
abstract: In quantum physics, the order in which different operations occur can be placed in superposition. The resulting processes have an indefinite causal order which is of fundamental interest and can be viewed as a novel quantum resource enabling new protocols. Here, we report an experimental proof-of-principle implementation of one such protocol, where we perform BB84-like quantum cryptography by placing Alice and Bob’s measurement-and-preparation operations in a photonic quantum SWITCH. By embedding Alice and Bob within the quantum SWITCH, the protocol achieves an average eavesdropper detection probability of 0.15 (0.02) per shared qubit, with eavesdropper detection performed through measurements of the control qubit rather than comparing the key. Unlike standard BB84 and related schemes, which detect eavesdropping by publicly revealing and discarding a fraction of the raw key, our approach requires no disclosure of key material: every retained qubit can, in principle, be tested for eavesdropping while remaining available for key generation. Although the present implementation does not yet constitute a secure quantum key distribution protocol, owing to post-selection required for measurements within the quantum SWITCH, it provides a proof of principle that indefinite causal order can be exploited to detect eavesdropping without sacrificing key bits.

title: Detection Of Novel Cyber Attacks In Telecommunication Networks Using Federated Learning Models
abstract: Zero-day cyber threats are a novel factor that puts modern telecommunication networks such as 5G/6G infrastructures and Core IP Multimedia Subsystems (IMS) under unprecedented operational risks. The existing centralized Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are based on raw telemetry collected from the network being analyzed and transferred to the cloud with massive communication latency, high bandwidth consumption, and serious lack of data-privacy. This research proposes the Federated Learning (FL) framework, a novel idea for building a decentralized security design with privacy protection capability to detect novel cyber attacks for distributed telecommunication infrastructures. The framework ensures strict localization of the sensitive network telemetry by executing the local deep learning inference and model training process on distributed edge nodes e.g., gNodeB base stations and edge gateways, while also collaboratively training a global anomaly detection model using privacy-preserving model aggregation. Empirical testing indicates that the proposed federated architecture attained a 98.45% threat detection accuracy and False Positive Rate (FPR) of 1.15%, and also reduced the bandwidth requirement of the wide area network by 84.2% over the one directly based on the centralized pipeline.

title: Cross-Domain Behavioural Mapping for IoT Attack Detection in Educational Networks Using CICIoT-2023 Dataset
venue: Indian Journal of Science and Technology
abstract: Objectives: The study develops a cross-domain behavioural intrusion-detection framework for transferring attack knowledge from CICIoT-2023 to a derived educational IoT representation. Method: The proposed Cross-Domain Behavioural Mapping Intrusion Detection System (CDBM-IDS) integrates an Educational IoT Digital Twin Layer (E-DTL), Behaviour Spectrum Encoder (BSE), Hierarchical Deviance Encoder (HDE), Tri-Context Fusion (TCF), and Sector-Transfer Consistency Loss (STC-Loss). EduTwin is generated from CICIoT-2023 through educational device-role mapping, interaction modelling, and sector-oriented behavioural transformation. Findings: Under the controlled EduTwin evaluation protocol, CDBM-IDS achieves 98.72% accuracy, 98.64% precision, 98.51% recall, 98.57% F1-score, and 99.21% AUC-ROC. Ablation analysis confirms measurable contributions from BSE, HDE, TCF, and STC-Loss. Novelty: The framework introduces educational role abstraction, frequency-domain behavioural encoding, hierarchical deviation modelling, geometric context fusion, and consistency-driven sector mapping. Keywords: IoT security, educational network, intrusion detection, cross-domain learning, behaviour modelling

title: Adaptive AI Framework for Real-Time Threat Detection in IoT Ecosystems
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems have seen rapid growth, and this growth has led to a significantly broader cyber attack surface to which the resource-constrained edge devices are targeted. The traditional centralized detection systems result in high bandwidth, long transmission delay and privacy concerns. Deplotting Machine Learning models at the network edge is the solution to dealing with latency; static edge model quickly gets stale from concept drift and can have challenges in detecting zero-day exploits. In addition, Fine Tune Edge models dynamically often results in catastrophic forgetting, leading to a high False Positive Rate (FPR). In this paper, we propose a lightweight Adaptive AI Framework for Real-Time Threat Detection in IoT Ecosystems in order to overcome such challenges. The framework is deployed at the edge layer, and runs with an 8-bit quantized neural engine as well as an Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) based Continual Learning (CL) mechanism. This architecture provides a low latency processing of network streams, realtime update of security models and allows maintenance of previous "benign" baselines without dependence on cloud. Empirical experiments conducted on benchmark datasets namely N-BaIoT and Edge-IIoTset with an ARM-based edge gateway shows that the proposed framework achieves an overall detection accuracy of 98.88%, F1 score of 98.75% and False Positive Rate of 1.20%. Critically, has very low memory usage (<16 MB) and low to average latency on the average (2.95 ms) on every compute. The results shows that the framework is effective, highly adaptable and of great scalability in the context of resource constrained IoT application environment. The main use cases covered include: IoT Security, Edge AI, Continual Learning, Elastic Weight Consolidation, Threat Detection, Low Latency, Concept Drift.

title: AI-Enhanced Fractal Network Protocol Steganography: A 2025 Framework for Covert and Adaptive Data Hiding in Digital Infrastructures
abstract: Network protocol steganography is a matured technology that can be used to encode information in regular communication traffic. But the existing embedding system built on static packet modification or field substitution is susceptible to AI-based traffic analysis and digital forensics. In this paper, we present an intelligent AI-Enhanced Fractal Network Steganography (AI-FNS) system that leverages fractal embedding theory, adaptive protocol manipulation, and deep learning-based traffic optimization to adaptively perform information hiding. The design employs a fractal self-similarity modeling based system that encodes a covert payload on three layers of a protocol stack (TCP/IP/ICMP) coupled with a generative adversarial learning system, which modifies the signatures of generated packets to resemble those of genuine network traffic. A second digital fingerprint verification module ensures the payload's integrity and authenticity using entropybalancing hashes. Experimental validation, the robustness and the robustness and effectiveness on a simulated enterprise network environment (10 GbE backbone). When the active intrusion detection and the steganalysis engines, AI-FNS has the packet detection rate < 1.4 %, PSNR = 54.2 dB, Bit Error Rate = 0.0021 and AI adaptation accuracy = 98.7 %. As compared with the conventional ICMP and DNS covert channels, the proposed model attains the 37 % in robustness, 42 % in detection probability and real-time embedding with low latency (< 3 ms per packet). Such results demonstrate the suitability of AI-FNS as a 2025 information abstraction model for secure, intelligent, and adaptive covert comm over digital networks.

title: AI-Driven Cybersecurity Framework for Modern Information Systems: Threat Detection and Risk Governance
abstract: The ever-growing number of zero-day attacks and functional disconnection between technical threat telemetry and corporate risk governance make modern enterprise information systems a tough nutritional challenge in terms of security. The problem of high False Positive Rates (FPR) with traditional Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems has resulted in alert fatigue and late responses to incidents. The authors of this paper put forward an AI-powered, integrated cybersecurity framework to combine real-time machine learning threat detection with automated risk governance. The proposed framework uses two-stage hybrid machine learning pipeline: unsupervised anomaly detection using the Isolation Forests method and supervised methods of ensemble learning (XGBoost/LSTM) for classifying the threat, by reducing FPR and conserving high DPR. Additionally, an algorithmic risk-scoring engine can plot a specific technical IoC directly to a corporate asset value, thereby aligning technical Indicators of Compromise direct to international regulatory compliance framework such as ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF. When tested on standardized benchmark datasets (CICIDS2017 and UNSW-NB15), the framework correctly detected 98.6% with only 42% fewer false positive alert messages than conventional baseline models. The findings show the strong benefits of bringing together real-time AI analytics and automated GRC mapping for continuous risk visibility, helping to dramatically reduce Mean Time to Respond (MTTR), and eliminating compliance drift in complex hybrid environments.

title: Formalized threshold reversible hiding in encrypted images in Post-Quantum settings
abstract: Abstract As advancements in computer vision emerge, the necessity for securing image processing techniques also arises. For this purpose, one of the promising methods is Reversible Data Hiding in Encrypted Images (RDHEI), which directly secures visual data while providing the option of embedding auxiliary information. However, RDHEI has not been formalized in the cryptographic context. The absence of such formalization leads to a lack of provable security guarantees and robust privacy comparisons between schemes. In this work, we address this gap by formalizing RDHEI, where we formally define the syntax, correctness properties, and security notions, including semantic security, payload privacy, separability, compactness, and robustness. Then, we construct Post-Quantum RDHEI (PQ-RDHEI) as an efficient scheme secure against quantum adversaries under the Module Learning With Errors assumption in the quantum random oracle model. Our design uses a Module Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism, pseudorandom functions, hash functions, and verifiable secret sharing as building blocks. The quantitative experiments show that on the standard grayscale test images, our PQ-RDHEI achieves embedding rates of 0.61-2.27 bits per pixel against 0.04-0.18 bits per pixel for the most efficient existing scheme, along with a $$13.4\times $$ improvement in mean rate, and raises the entropy of the encrypted shares from 7.48 to 7.9902-7.9992 bits per pixel.

title: Evaluation of cybersecurity awareness among high school students in Turkey before and after training
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has increased young users’ exposure to online threats and has made the need for effective cybersecurity education at the secondary school level more apparent. This study examines cybersecurity awareness among high school students and evaluates a structured training program implemented in four different types of high schools in the Darica district of Turkey. Data were collected with a five-point Likert-type survey before and after the training. The 601 students who were present in both measurements formed the dataset used for the pre-post analysis. The awareness scale was examined through principal component analysis which yielded a five-dimensional structure with acceptable overall internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.86). Individual-level change was analyzed with paired-samples t-tests and Cohen’s d. Differences by school, grade and gender were tested with analysis of variance and independent-samples t-tests. Finally, students’ ability to distinguish genuine from fraudulent website screenshots was examined with McNemar tests. Before the training, male students and students in academically selective and technically oriented schools showed higher awareness on several dimensions. After the training scores for action-oriented protective behaviors rose, while self-reported scores on the conceptual-knowledge dimensions declined. One possible interpretation is that students formed a more realistic view of their own knowledge rather than losing it, though this was not tested directly. Recognition of several fraudulent pages improved, for example from 50.4% to 63.9% on one item, although accuracy on the genuine pages did not increase. On some dimensions differences between schools and between genders were smaller after the training, while on others they persisted. Since the study compared matched participants without a control group these results are interpreted as changes associated with the training rather than as definitive proof of cause. Overall, the findings indicate that standardized, school-wide cybersecurity training was associated with changes in students’ protective behavior and in their recognition of several fraudulent pages and they support integrating such programs into secondary education. Clinical trial number : Not applicable.

title: Dynamic weighted federated contrastive learning for robust medical image classification under heterogeneous data
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, AI-driven medical image classification has attracted considerable attention in recent years. However, increasingly stringent data privacy regulations have significantly restricted data sharing among medical institutions, making it difficult for traditional centralized learning frameworks to effectively exploit distributed medical data resources. As a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, federated learning enables multiple institutions to collaboratively train models without directly exchanging raw data.
